items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to implementing the
"New York State Build Public Renewables Act"
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4134

SPONSOR: PARKER
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public authorities law, in relation to implementing
the "New York State Build Public Renewables Act"

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To enable the New York Power Authority (NYPA) to own and build new
renewable generation, storage, and transmission, require NYPA to provide
only renewable energy by 2030 and to provide renewable energy to all
state owned and municipal properties by 2035. The legislation lays the
groundwork for the transition to a renewable, democratically controlled,
publicly owned energy system New York needs in order to meet the goals
of the landmark Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act and lead
the nation on climate.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

This legislation amends Section 1005 of the public authorities law by
adding new subdivisions 30 through 43. Key provisions are as follows:
Subdivision 30 gives the New York Power Authority the authority and
directive to purchase, acquire, plan, design, engineer, finance,
construct, operate, manage, improve and maintain any renewable energy
project, and to provide energy efficiency, retrofits, high
performance/sustainable building, and energy management services.
Subdivision 32 requires that NYPA only own, build and maintain energy
generation, storage and transmission that is renewable by 2030. The
Authority is directed to phase out all existing non-renewable generation
as soon as is feasible. It also outlines how certain renewable energy
sources will be prioritized.

Subdivision 33 outlines how NYPA will maintain transparency, which
includes requiring a ten-year climate and resiliency plan to be made
public within two years with a minimum of eight public hearings within
that time frame. It also requires that the authority submit an annual
report to the governor and legislature to be made publicly available and
outlines the contents of the report. Additionally, the Authority will be
required to present a public democratization plan within 2 years of the
effective date.

Subdivision 34 establishes that NYPA will be the sole electricity and
power provider to all state properties by 2030. For municipal owned,
leased, controlled or operated properties, NYPA will be the sole provid-
er by 2035, however municipalities may opt out for buildings where the
energy supply rate for NYPA is higher than another local utility, or a
building is being served by another utility providing renewable energy,
or the building is participating in a community choice aggregate program
that supplies renewable energy.

Subdivision 35 authorizes the Authority to provide renewable energy to
residential customers and CCA communities with the requirement that
energy supply above what is required for public buildings be sold first
to low-and moderate-income households at a rate 50% lower than that
provided by local utilities. It also authorizes NYPA to sell up to thir-
ty percent of its electricity to the long island power authority.

Subdivisions 36 through 43 establish labor and procurement standards.
All NYPA projects are defined as "public" with the labor protections
that this requires and the provisions provide for a "transition fund"
funded by NYPA to train impacted NYPA employees. Other labor provisions
protect existing workers from displacement and from any changes to
existing rights and benefits. Employees who have lost their jobs in the
"non-renewable sector" will get priority for jobs with NYPA projects and
NYPA is required to work on job development prograMs / apprenticeships
with unions and community-based organizations. The legislation provides
for prioritization for hiring of NYCHA residents in NYPA projects at
NYCHA. The legislation also includes buy America procurement provisions
as well as provisions to ensure NYPA's compliance with and participation
in state minority and women-owned business and service-disabled veterans
business programs.

Section 3 expands NYPA trustees from 7 to 17 with the 10 additional
members appointed 2 by governor, 4 by president of the Senate, and 4 by
speaker of the assembly based on recommendations by labor, advocates,
experts, and people identified by clean energy hubs.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

With the passage of the landmark Climate Leadership and Community
Protection Act in 2019, New York has committed to moving away from non-
renewable energy generation and relying entirely on renewable sources.
In order to achieve this, New York needs capable public ownership of its
energy generation, transmission and distribution. Currently, NYPA is
unable to own, build or maintain new renewable energy generation
projects. This bill will give them the power to do so, ensuring that our
transition to renewable energy is in capable hands. It will enable New
York to fully power State and municipal properties and transportation
with renewable energy by 2035, an important step in minimizing our
carbon footprint. NYPA will be able to sell renewable energy directly to
all of its customers, and low-income customers' rate will be less than
the rate of their current utility. This bill will also create new green
jobs, as well as helping people who previously worked in non-renewable
energy to transition to new jobs in sustainable energy. All employees
will be paid a prevailing wage and be subject to project labor agree-
ments. New York needs to provide good jobs for people in a growing
industry. NYPA is the largest publicly owned utility in the country and
has proven itself by providing the most affordable energy in New York
State. This bill will put the massive and important prosp ect of
converting to renewable energy in capable hands.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE. HISTORY:

2021-22: S6453C - Passed Senate

2019-20: S7232 - Referred to Energy and Telecommunications

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately

summary: Implements the "New York State Build Public Renewables Act"; requires the New York power authority to provide only renewable energy and power to customers; requires such authority to be the sole provider of energy to all state owned and municipal properties; requires certain New York power authority projects and programs pay a prevailing wage and utilize project labor agreements.
title: Implements the "New York State Build Public Renewables Act"
